text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH for Silverline (tenant: slv) — private VPC egress failing to external model endpoints via NLB. Error rate spike + DNS NXDOMAINs from tenant side. auto-escalate: oncall

anya (SRE): getting the page. seeing 502s and lots of connection resets from the NLB. customers reporting timeouts to api.external-models.net :
- 502 from NLB
- intermittent DNS failures for model endpoints

darren (oncall): acknowledged. paging netops + customer-eng. @maria can you check NLB target health and SG changes? @kevin pls ping Silverline SRE for any recent firewall changes

maria (netops): on it. checking target group health now
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/slv-nlb-tg
```

maria (netops): target health: some targets unhealthy (502) but majority healthy. health check latency spiking. no config push in last 30m in our audit logs.

silverline-sre: we didn't change anything on our side. we see DNS NXDOMAINs intermittently for api.external-models.net around the same time. our NAT gateway logs show lots of ephemeral port reuse.

anya (SRE): possible conntrack / ephemeral exhaustion on customer NAT or misrouted traffic. can you run `curl -v https://api.external-models.net/health` from a host in the VPC?

silverline-sre: attaching results: `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: api.external-models.net` then later `curl: (52) Empty reply from server`

darren (oncall): ok plausible multi-pronged: DNS resolution failures + some backends returning empty/502. plan: 1) add temporary DNS fallback to our hosted model egress for that tenant 2) enable NLB connection draining reduction? 3) ask Silverline to check NAT conntrack table 4) create short-term route to our regional transit to bypass their NAT path

kevin (customer-eng): asked Silverline to run `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` and `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` — waiting on numbers.

silverline-sre: conntrack count = 65534, max = 65536. we hit the ceiling and are dropping new connections. no recent policy changes.

anya (SRE): that explains it — conntrack exhaustion causing DNS failures and incomplete TCP handshakes -> 502/empty replies. immediate mitigation: recommend Silverline increase nf_conntrack_max and flush stale conntrack entries. Also we will add a temporary routing fallback for their tenant to our hosted egress pool so they can reach model endpoints while they remediate.

darren (oncall): maria, can you apply the routing override for tenant slv to route egress through rwi-egress-proxy in us-east-1 (best-effort) for next 30m and set a TTL in the routing policy? keep me posted.

maria (netops): preparing route pin. applying now.
```
# apply policy (internal control plane)
POST /api/v1/tenants/slv/routing
{ "egress_route": "rwi-egress-proxy-us-east-1", "priority": 900, "expires_at": "2418206799" }
```

maria (netops): applied. verified via traceroute from a test pod in tenant VPC: now traversing rwi-egress-proxy.

anya (SRE): kevin — tell Silverline to run `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and `sudo conntrack -F` (careful — this will drop existing connections). advise maintenance window but given severity ok to proceed.

silverline-sre: increasing now. will flush after ramp. doing `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144`

silverline-sre: flushed conntrack. testing... `curl -v https://api.external-models.net/health` -> 200 OK. DNS resolution fixed from hosts that had resolved failures.

kevin (customer-eng): Silverline reports restoration to service for their traffic routed via our fallback egress. they will keep increased conntrack and monitor. planning patch to tune application connection reuse to reduce table pressure.

darren (oncall): good. next steps: 1) create incident ticket INC-2418204829 with timeline & mitigation 2) keep route override for 2 hours then automatic rollback 3) follow up with Silverline on conntrack tuning & long-term NAT capacity 4) run post-incident review for NLB health-check sensitivity vs conntrack symptoms

anya (SRE): filing incident now. adding initial severity: P1 customer impact (enterprise dedicated VPC). tagging: vpc, nlb, dns, conntrack, routing-fallback
```
/incident create --title "Silverline VPC egress: conntrack exhaustion causing DNS/502" --severity P1 --assignees anya,darren,maria,kevin --tenant slv
```

maria (netops): will monitor NLB metrics and error rates. setting alert for spike to >3% 502s for 15m.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2418204829 created by anya (SRE). Pager cleared for oncall after mitigation.

kevin (customer-eng): Silverline escalation contact confirmed: lena@silverline.io — they'll open a postmortem on their side and coordinate with us.

darren (oncall): I'll keep watch for 45m then hand back to triage. thanks all. :thumbsup:

anya (SRE): adding runbook note: when tenant VPC sees DNS NXDOMAIN + 502s concurrently, check conntrack immediately; consider temporary egress reroute to hosted pool to minimize customer outage. adding to runbook repo.

maria (netops): metrics look stable. closing in 30.

(20:40) end of thread: last state = mitigated, temporary route expires at 2418206799, follow-up task created: TASK-2418204835 (postmortem + customer coordination)
